newsitem.title: GERMANY: Allianz not actively seeking French partner.
newsitem.headline: Allianz not actively seeking French partner.

text.p: German insurance group Allianz is not in active talks to seek a French partner after it was displaced from Europe's number-one position by the recent merger of Axa SA and UAP, Allianz chief executive Henning Schulte-Noelle said on Wednesday.
Asked whether Allianz intended to take over French insurer AGF, he said "There are no concrete talks."
But he added that Allianz was looking to build its presence in France over the long term.
Allianz not actively seeking French partner

Schulte-Noelle told a news conference that losing its position as Europe's largest insurer would not have any direct impact on Allianz's business, although the number-one tag was valuable as a sales and marketing tool.

"I would rather be number one than number two -- you cannot dispute that the number one position has a value for marketing," Schulte-Noelle said after speaking at an economic conference at Cologne university.

He said that the unified Axa and UAP would take time to combine their resources and match the profitability and share rating of Allianz -- which he said were both twice as high as the French competitor.
But the merged Axa UAP would not pose any direct new threat in Allianz's home market in Germany, because they were already represented by their subsidiary CKAG Colonia, he said.
That said, Schulte-Noelle said the French challenge should not be underestimated: "We face a very strong competitor."
